correctness.rationale: Positive: maximal pairwise disjoint quota supports require at most n/q<=k candidates and intersect every quota support; padding maintains JR. Negative: the 4-copy reduction makes q=4 and the shared dummy represents every eligible candidate, leaving only e as the JR test. For any allocation of 4t triples among four copies, each t-allocation in a NO X3C instance misses >=1, each underallocation t-b misses >=3b. Deficit total B=0 misses >=4; B=1 misses >=5; B>=2 misses >=6. The YES construction covers all. NP membership follows by direct verification of supporter counts and each candidate's unrepresented supporters. The standalone exact finite checks were executed and match the proof; they do not establish the all-size theorem.

value.rationale: A natural exact support-size boundary for a very recent social-choice axiom: it separates a guaranteed constructive subdomain from NP-complete feasibility by the addition of a single unselectable but JR-blocking candidate. The common-dummy and all-but-one support constraints isolate the source of computational hardness instead of merely repeating unrestricted X3C hardness. Such structurally sharp complexity boundaries inform domain restrictions and algorithms for group-diverse committee selection.
